To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of ontologies and the Semantic Web is an effective means of enabling the integration of heterogeneous data sources and the use of data from multiple disciplines.

the semantic web is the most appropriate technology for eScience, that the Semantic Web for Earth and Environmental Terminology (SWEET) is the best available ontology, that the Semantic Sensor Web is a promising new application area, and that a semantic web-based eScience infrastructure is feasible.

the Semantic Web can be used to encode the meaning of data in science and that it is the most promising approach for doing so, given its extensibility, openness, and ability to be integrated with other technologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to make sense of data in eScience.

the problem of how to enable scientists and engineers to work with data and information from other disciplines and other sources in order to facilitate interdisciplinary and cross-disciplinary science and engineering, and to enable scientists to use information from other sources to support their own research.
the problem of how to make sense of data, how to understand it, how to use it, and, in the case of data generated by others, how to understand its meaning and use it in our own context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of data-intensive science, or e-Science, is not yet ready to meet the demands of the modern world.
data is not the problem.
eScience has not yet reached its full potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to answer the questions " What do these data mean?"
we need to be able to "understand" data.
we are developing a system that can be used to encode meaning in scientific data and that this system is designed to be used by scientists, not data experts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data-intensive nature of eScience, and the increasing use of data and information products in science, is creating a need for a new approach to data management.
the semantic web can provide a solution to these problems.
we can no longer afford to ignore the semantic aspects of science.
